title: Entanglement-assisted remote energy transfer
authors: Bashir Mojaveri, Rasoul Jafarzadeh Bahrbeig, Mohammad Ali Fasihi, Nasrin Abdi
abstract: Currently, remote energy transfer and immunity to dissipation are hot topics in quantum batteries (QBs). In this work, we propose a protocol to realize energy transfer between two remote atoms (a quantum charger and a quantum battery) each coupled to a separate optical cavity with the cavities connected by a fiber. The cavities and fiber are coupled to their individual baths. After optimizing inter-system couplings to achieve an efficient transfer, we uncover the effect of suppressing dissipation by introducing parity deformation of the cavities fields. We also prove that the charger-battery entanglement is a consumable resource for energy storage: it is initially stored until the charger and battery reach energy balance, and then subsequently consumed to maintain the increase in energy stored in the battery. The present scheme is the first execution of energy transfer to a distant battery assisted by entanglement, which may help better understand quantum thermodynamics and open new possibilities toward harnessing decoherence as a resource to improve the charging performance of QBs.
summary: The paper presents a novel protocol for remotely charging a quantum battery using entanglement assistance across two cavities connected by an optical fiber. By employing parity deformation of the cavity fields, the researchers suppress environmental dissipation while demonstrating that initial entanglement acts as a consumable resource to maximize stored energy. This offers new insights into harnessing decoherence effects in quantum thermodynamics.
main_problem: The work proposes a protocol for entanglement-assisted remote energy transfer between two distant atoms (charger and battery) coupled to separate optical cavities.
main_result: High-efficiency charging is achieved by introducing parity deformation of the cavity fields, which suppresses dissipation. Furthermore, initial charger-battery entanglement is shown to be a consumable resource necessary to maintain increased stored energy in the battery.
method: The analysis uses the para-Bose algebra formalism and solves the open system dynamics governed by a Markovian master equation under Born-Markov approximations.
model_or_system: The physical model consists of two distant two-level atoms, each coupled to an optical cavity, with the cavities linked by a fiber. The entire setup is treated as an open quantum system interacting with bosonic reservoirs (baths).
key_observables: Energy Transfer Efficiency, Stored Energy ($\Delta E_B$), Extractable Work (Ergotropy), and the degree of entanglement.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the short fiber limit, the Born-Markov approximation, and the use of the para-Bose algebra to model cavity field interactions.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical system, develops the Hamiltonian using parity-deformed fields, derives the master equation, solves the resulting differential equations for key observables, and finally analyzes how entanglement consumption drives enhanced energy storage.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses advanced topics in open quantum systems, specifically leveraging non-standard algebraic structures (para-Bose algebra) to control decoherence and enhance energy transfer—a critical area in quantum thermodynamics and cavity QED.
